I'm reviewing PR #27 on the lgriffin/TER repository. I need to examine the benchmark/sample data files for sensitive content.

Run these commands to get patches:

```bash
gh api repos/lgriffin/TER/pulls/27/files --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.filename | test("^benchmarks/")) | .patch'
```

- benchmarks/annotations/mock_annotations.csv (5 lines added)
- benchmarks/annotations/session-001.csv (14 lines added)
- benchmarks/example_annotations.jsonl (6 lines added)
- benchmarks/example_annotations_candidate.jsonl (6 lines added)
- benchmarks/mock_benchmark.jsonl (4 lines added)
- benchmarks/pilot_annotations.jsonl (13 lines added)
- benchmarks/tool_call_adversarial.jsonl (7 lines added)

Check for:
1. Any real API keys, tokens, or secrets
2. Any real usernames, email addresses, or PII
3. Any real file paths that could reveal infrastructure details
4. Any real conversation content that should be anonymized
5. Is the data well-structured and consistent?

Report findings as a structured list with file, severity (critical/warning/info), and description.
